bug_info.bug_desc: In the address assembly logic, the early word-aligned and halfword-aligned address calculations use addr_q[31:8] as the high part of the next address. At the time addr_ready_in_word or addr_ready_in_halfword is asserted, addr_q has not yet latched the final incoming address byte, so only the lower 24 bits of addr_q contain previously latched address data. Bits [31:24] are still stale/uninitialized, causing the assembled SRAM/read address to be wrong and potentially causing an incorrect data region or mailbox selection. The correct source for the already-latched bytes is addr_q[23:0].
bug_info.fix_hint: Change both early address mux branches to use addr_q[23:0] instead of addr_q[31:8] when concatenating the previously latched address bytes with the partial byte currently being received from the serial-to-parallel converter. This preserves the three already-latched address bytes and keeps the early read request address consistent with the final full address.
